messages:
marco: FYI, dashboards showing a sudden rise in 429s for embeddings.v1 in us-west-2 starting ~10m ago. Rerank traffic steady but the embeddings lane queue is spiking and hitting the soft admission limit.

sara: ugh, saw that. any deploys or config changes?

anthony: no deploys on serving in last hour. infra alert fired for queue depth. digging into admission controller logs now.

ops-bot: Incident detected: embeddings-pool-usw queue_depth > 90% for 8m. Auto-scaling not triggered due to capacity cap = 12 gpus.

elena: Could be warmup churn — a bunch of small embed requests from a customer burst. Those are chewing KV cache and blocking bigger batches.

raj: Are embeddings and rerank sharing the same egress fabric or token budget? We split lanes but admission control still uses a shared global token window in the policy engine.

anthony: confirmed — policy-config still has shared_token_window: true for region us-west-2. That causes embeddings to be rate-limited whenever overall token consumption is high.

marco: That's the problem then. We intended separate token windows for emb vs rerank. How bad is impact?

anthony: 429s ~ 4x baseline for embeddings, tail latency for accepted requests up ~120ms. Most are small vector calls but high qps so queueing wins.

elena: Quick mitigation: flip shared_token_window to false for us-west-2 so lanes enforce independent softlimits. Should be safe for a short window.

raj: Add a guard — while we make change, reduce embeddings admission_priority from medium->high? That will let embeddings through but may starve rerank. Probably prefer embeddings because customer-facing search is broken.

marco: We should avoid starving rerank. Suggested: set independent windows and small safety headroom: embeddings_window=0.7*pool_tokens, rerank_window=0.25*pool_tokens, leftover for misc = 0.05.

anthony: I can roll config now. Planning command: 
```
rbctl region apply --region=us-west-2 --set policy.shared_token_window=false 
rbctl region apply --region=us-west-2 --set policy.embeddings_window=0.7 
rbctl region apply --region=us-west-2 --set policy.rerank_window=0.25
```

ops-bot: Note: applying region policy will cause a quick re-sync across 24 policy nodes, expected <30s convergence.

sara: If we change windows, do we need to scale the embeddings pool? The cap at 12 GPUs might still bottleneck.

anthony: After flip, monitor for a minute. If queue depth stays >80% we'll hit emergency scale. I have a one-off script to bump reserved-capacity for embeddings pool: 
```
rlsctl bump-capacity --pool embeddings-usw --delta 4 --reason "auto-mitigation"
```
But that requires approval from platform-ops or a commit in the autoscale policy.

elena: We could also enable short-lived packing of quantized-vectors for cheap customers: fallback_model=embedding-small-8bit for low-priority qps. Lowers GPU time.

marco: Let's do config flip now, then watch. If still hot, run bump-capacity (anthony gets sign-off). Also add a temporary admission rule to drop extremely tiny spammy requests (size < 16 tokens & qps > 200) — that reduces churn.

anthony: Applying now.

ops-bot: rbctl apply accepted. Policy change initiated. Convergence ETA 24s.

anthony: policy change converged. embedding 429s dropped 60% within 90s. queue depth decreased to ~45%. tail p95 latency back to normal.

marco: Nice. Leave independent windows for 24h and let autoscaler evaluate. Create a follow-up to revisit token-window defaults.

raj: Agreed. I'll open a runbook PR to document independent lane windows and the spillover heuristic. Tagging platform-ops for autoscale permission flow.

sara: Also recommend we add a lightweight per-customer QPS limiter to avoid noisy tenants causing region-level churn.

marco: Good call. Thanks all. Marking this resolved for now. :thumbsup:
